topic: Research: Groq API Guide 2026: Fastest LLM Inference for Developers (Free Tier Included)

key_points: Benchmarks show Groq Llama 3.1 8B around 750 T/s vs GPT-4o mini 110 T/s and GPT-4o 63 T/s
Highlights TTFT and model-cost differences with Groq focused on speed while OpenAI leads on frontier reasoning
Recommends a practical split stack: Groq for latency-critical flows and OpenAI for quality-heavy use cases
Positions Groq as strong on ultra-fast latency and cheaper open-model inference
States Groq only supports open-source model lineups while OpenAI provides proprietary models and broader tooling
Framing is architecture-centric: using Groq for streaming/voice/high-volume and OpenAI for richer reasoning-heavy tasks
Claims Groq’s LPU is 3–10x lower latency than GPU inference on Fireworks in many scenarios
Notes a pricing advantage on Llama 3.1 8B at $0.05/$0.08 per 1M input/output versus higher Fireworks tiers
Highlights model breadth tradeoff: Fireworks supports a larger catalog and fine-tuning options while Groq has lower latency and discount features
Gives concrete TTFT comparisons: Groq Llama 3.3 70B ~0.3–0.5s at short prompts vs Fireworks ~0.8–1.2s
Shows context sensitivity: Groq remains materially faster at 128K context windows in published benchmark walkthrough
Useful migration guidance by pairing speed outcomes with deployment and workload fit rather than raw cost alone
Frames Groq vs Cerebras as high-speed open-weights inferencing providers with different token throughput and pricing curves
Compares flagship model economics: Groq about $0.59/$0.79 per 1M tokens vs Cerebras about $0.85/$1.20 for Groq-like Llama 3.3 70B
Highlights model-access implication: neither platform hosts GPT/Claude/Gemini, so both are positioned for open-weights stacks

stats.fact: Groq lists official pricing for Llama 3.1 8B at $0.05/$0.08 input/output per 1M tokens, Llama 4 Scout at $0.11/$0.34, and Llama 3.3 70B at $0.59/$0.79.
Groq public pricing page advertises fast model rates including 594 TPS for Llama 4 Scout and 840 TPS for Llama 3.1 8B Instant, with a 50% Batch API discount for async workloads.
Groq rate-limits are defined across request, token, audio and context metrics and include Free, Developer, and enterprise tiers; headers expose remaining request/token counters for runtime control.
TokenMix-style consolidated reference indicates Groq free-tier defaults of 30 RPM, 6,000 TPM, and 1,000 RPD for most models, with tighter caps for some larger MoE models (e.g., Llama 4 Maverick).

Groq's official docs describe the service as OpenAI-compatible via `https://api.groq.com/openai/v1`, with unsupported features still present (e.g., `logprobs`, `logit_bias`, `top_logprobs`, some audio transcript formats).

OpenAI API pricing currently includes GPT-5.5 at $5.00/$30.00 input/output per 1M tokens, GPT-5.4 at $2.50/$15.00, and GPT-5.4 mini at $0.75/$4.50, giving a premium-quality alternative point for comparison.

angles: Position Groq as a speed-first open-weights inference layer: sub-200ms TTFT for many prompts changes UX in chat/voice/chatbot, but quality tradeoffs vs closed models remain explicit
Build a production routing strategy, not a winner/loser story: use Groq for latency-sensitive tasks and OpenAI for deep reasoning or proprietary model features
Treat free-tier limits as the real gate, not headline model speed — 30 RPM/1,000 RPD constraints push many teams to hybrid or fallback providers
Use Batch API + prompt caching as a cost lever for non-realtime workloads while keeping Groq for interactive endpoints
Frame compatibility as a migration asset: OpenAI-style clients and base URL minimize lock-in, but unsupported params can still break compatibility assumptions
Compare Groq against both GPU-era incumbents and other inference-specialist chips (Fireworks/Cerebras) using latency-at-context-depth, pricing per million, and model coverage
